question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -15 \\ -17\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
.
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -15 \\ -17\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -15 \\ -17\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -15 \\ -17\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-5 \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-15 \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-17\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the second and the third equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8{x}_{1} &=-32 \\ {x}_{1} &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=-4$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-17 \\ 4(-4)+{x}_{2} &=-17 \\ {x}_{2} &=-1 \\ {x}_{2} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-4$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-5 \\ (-4)+2(-1) &=-5 \\ -6 &=-5\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 21\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 21\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 21\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 21\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-9 \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-7 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=21\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} &=-16 \\ {x}_{2} &=8\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=8$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-9 \\ {x}_{1}-(8) &=-9 \\ {x}_{1} &=-1 \\ {x}_{1} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=8$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=21 \\ 2(-1)+3(8) &=21 \\ 22 &=21\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ -{x}_{2} &=-4 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=4$.

Substituting ${x}_{2}=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ 3{x}_{1}-8(4) &=-14 \\ 3{x}_{1} &=18 \\ {x}_{1} &=6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=4 \\ -2(6)+4(4) &=4 \\ 4 &=4\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=4$, which means

$$
6{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(6)+(4)=10.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-6 \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} &=-4 \\ {x}_{2} &=2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-6 \\ {x}_{1}-(2) &=-6 \\ {x}_{1} &=-4 \\ {x}_{1} &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-4$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ 2(-4)+3(2) &=-2 \\ -2 &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-4$ and ${x}_{2}=2$, which means

$$
-4{a}_{1}+2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-4)+(2)=-2.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=6 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=3 \\ {x}_{2} &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation we get ${x}_{2}=2$.

Substituting ${x}_{2}=2$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=3 \\ -{x}_{1}+(2) &=3 \\ -{x}_{1} &=1 \\ {x}_{1} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=6 \\ -(-1)+2(2) &=6 \\ 5 &=6\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.
